blocks.text: When two bodies travelling along an axis do not end up travelling along the same initial axis after the collision, it is a case of a two-dimensional collision. When the collision is elastic, the system of bodies conserves both its total linear momentum and its total kinetic energy. Consider two bodies colliding elastically at a certain glancing angle, so that the collision is not head-on. Let m1 be the mass of the first body (the projectile) moving with initial velocity v1i, and m2 the mass of the second body (the target), initially at rest, v2i = 0. As the two bodies collide, the impulses generated between them send them off at angles theta1 and theta2 to the x-axis along which the projectile initially travelled (Fig. 2.15).

blocks.alt: x and y axes with ball m2 at rest at the origin. Ball m1 approaches along the x axis with velocity v1i. After the collision m1 moves off above the axis at angle theta1 with velocity v1f and m2 moves off below the axis at angle theta2 with velocity v2f.
blocks.caption: Elastic glancing collision in two dimensions (original diagram after Figure 2.15).

blocks.title: Glancing collision
blocks.text: An elastic collision that is not a head-on collision between two bodies; initially the target body of mass m2 is at rest.

The initial momentum of the projectile before the collision is m1 v1i, while the initial momentum of the target is zero. The final momentum of the projectile, of mass m1 and velocity v1f, is m1 v1f, and the final momentum of the target, of mass m2 and velocity v2f, is m2 v2f. Resolve the final momentum of the projectile into components m1 v1f cos theta1 and m1 v1f sin theta1, and that of the target into m2 v2f cos theta2 and m2 v2f sin theta2. Momentum conservation along the x-axis: momentum before = momentum after, m1 v1i = m1 v1f cos theta1 + m2 v2f cos theta2, or m1 v1i - m1 v1f cos theta1 = m2 v2f cos theta2 ... (2.34). Momentum conservation along the y-axis: 0 = m1 v1f sin theta1 - m2 v2f sin theta2, or m1 v1f sin theta1 = m2 v2f sin theta2 ... (2.35).

(1/2) m1 v1i^2 = (1/2) m1 v1f^2 + (1/2) m2 v2f^2, or m1 v1i^2 = m1 v1f^2 + m2 v2f^2 ... (2.36). Analysis of these equations reveals four unknown quantities, v1f, v2f, theta1 and theta2; if these quantities can be measured, conservation of momentum and energy can be proved using equations (2.34), (2.35) and (2.36).

Some of the kinetic energy is transferred into other forms such as heat, sound and deformation in an inelastic collision: a bullet fired into a block of wood loses energy as sound and heat, and a ball dropped on a floor from a height does not rebound to the same height because kinetic energy is lost in other forms such as sound and heat (Interesting Information).

blocks.title: Example 2.9 (printed after 2.12)
blocks.text: A particle A of mass 1 kg moving with initial velocity 5 m s^-1 towards the right collides with a stationary target B of the same mass. After the collision A moves at 30 degrees above the horizontal with a speed of 3 m s^-1 and B moves at 53 degrees with the horizontal with a speed of 4 m s^-1. Prove that the collision is elastic. Solution: initial momentum = m1 v1i + m2 v2i = (1 kg x 5 m s^-1) + (1 kg x 0) = 5 kg m s^-1. Final momentum in the x-direction = m1 v1f cos 30 + m2 v2f cos 53 = (1 kg x 3 m s^-1 x cos 30) + (1 kg x 4 m s^-1 x cos 53) = 2.60 + 2.40 = 5 kg m s^-1, so momentum is conserved in the x-direction. (KE)i = (1/2) x 1 x 5^2 + (1/2) x 1 x 0 = 12.5 J; (KE)f = (1/2) x 1 x 3^2 + (1/2) x 1 x 4^2 = 4.5 + 8 = 12.5 J. As both momentum and kinetic energy are conserved, the collision is elastic.

blocks.caption: The three equations of a glancing elastic collision
rows: m1 v1i = m1 v1f cos theta1 + m2 v2f cos theta2
m1 v1f sin theta1 = m2 v2f sin theta2

blocks.prompt: In Example 2.9, check momentum conservation along the y-axis as well, and say why kinetic energy did not need resolving into components.
blocks.explanation: y-momentum after: 1 x 3 x sin 30 - 1 x 4 x sin 53 = 1.50 - 3.19 = -1.7 kg m s^-1, which is not zero: with the printed angles the y-momentum is only approximately balanced, so the printed example checks x-momentum and energy only. Kinetic energy is a scalar, so the speeds are used directly in (1/2) m v^2 without components.

items: Glancing elastic collision, target at rest: x-momentum m1 v1i = m1 v1f cos theta1 + m2 v2f cos theta2; y-momentum m1 v1f sin theta1 = m2 v2f sin theta2; energy m1 v1i^2 = m1 v1f^2 + m2 v2f^2; four unknowns v1f, v2f, theta1, theta2.
